title: 04. AsyncIO: Async I/O Libraries

sections.title: 13.1 aiohttp — Async HTTP Client/Server
sections.body:

```

║                    AIOHTTP OVERVIEW                                         ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  Traditional (Synchronous) HTTP:                                            ║
║  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ ║
║  │ Request 1 ─────[wait]─────> Response 1                                │ ║

║  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ ║
║  │ Request 1 ─────┐                                                      │ ║
║  │ Request 2 ─────┼─────[await all]────> Responses                       │ ║
║  │ Request 3 ─────┘                                                      │ ║
║  │                                                                        │ ║
║  │ Total time: max(t1, t2, t3)                                           │ ║

║  │                                                                       │  ║
║  │    ┌─────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐                   │  ║
║  │    │   ClientSession  │         │   Application   │                   │  ║
║  │    │   (HTTP Client)  │         │  (HTTP Server)  │                   │  ║
║  │    │                  │         │                  │                   │  ║
║  │    │ • GET, POST...   │         │ • Routes         │                   │  ║
║  │    │ • Connection Pool│         │ • Middlewares    │                   │  ║
║  │    │ • Cookie Jar     │         │ • WebSocket      │                   │  ║
║  │    └─────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘                   │  ║
║  │                                                                       │  ║

║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic HTTP Client

```python
import aiohttp
import asyncio

async def fetch(session, url):
    """Fetch a single URL"""
    async with session.get(url) as response:
        status = response.status
        content = await response.text()
        return {'url': url, 'status': status, 'length': len(content)}

async def main():
    urls = [
        'http://example.com',
        'http://httpbin.org/get',
        'http://httpbin.org/headers',
    ]

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        # Fetch all URLs concurrently
        tasks = [fetch(session, url) for url in urls]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

        for result in results:
            print(f"{result['url']}: {result['status']}, {result['length']} bytes")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: HTTP Methods and Headers

```python
import aiohttp
import asyncio
import json

async def main():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        # GET with parameters
        params = {'key': 'value', 'page': 1}
        async with session.get('http://httpbin.org/get', params=params) as resp:
            data = await resp.json()
            print(f"GET args: {data['args']}")

        # POST with JSON
        payload = {'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30}
        async with session.post('http://httpbin.org/post', json=payload) as resp:
            data = await resp.json()
            print(f"POST json: {data['json']}")

        # POST with form data
        form_data = aiohttp.FormData()
        form_data.add_field('file', b'file content', filename='test.txt')
        async with session.post('http://httpbin.org/post', data=form_data) as resp:
            data = await resp.json()
            print(f"POST files: {list(data['files'].keys())}")

        # Custom headers
        headers = {'X-Custom-Header': 'custom-value'}
        async with session.get('http://httpbin.org/headers', headers=headers) as resp:
            data = await resp.json()
            print(f"Headers: {data['headers'].get('X-Custom-Header')}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 3: Session Configuration

```python
import aiohttp
import asyncio
from aiohttp import ClientTimeout

async def main():
    # Configure timeout
    timeout = ClientTimeout(total=30, connect=10, sock_read=10)

    # Configure connection pool
    connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(
        limit=100,          # Max total connections
        limit_per_host=10,  # Max connections per host
        ttl_dns_cache=300,  # DNS cache TTL
    )

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
        timeout=timeout,
        connector=connector,
        headers={'User-Agent': 'MyApp/1.0'},
    ) as session:

        # All requests use configured session
        async with session.get('http://example.com') as resp:
            print(f"Status: {resp.status}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: Reuse one ClientSession
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  app["Application start-up"] --> s["one aiohttp.ClientSession"]
  s --> pool[("connection pool — TCPConnector(limit=100)")]
  pool -->|"keep-alive reuse"| h1["api.example.com"]
  pool --> h2["auth.example.com"]
  r1["request 1"] --> s
  r2["request 2"] --> s
  r3["request N"] --> s
diagrams.explain: A session owns a **connection pool**; creating one per request throws away keep-alive connections and TLS handshakes and can leak sockets. Create one session at start-up, share it, close it at shutdown, and set the connector limit to cap concurrency per host.

sections.title: 13.2 aiofiles — Async File I/O
sections.body:
### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    AIOFILES                                                 ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  Traditional File I/O (blocking):                                           ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │    open()     read()      process     write()    close()            │   ║
║  │    ─────────[BLOCK]────────────────[BLOCK]─────────>                │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │    Event loop is blocked! No other coroutines can run.              │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  aiofiles (non-blocking):                                                   ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │    await open()  await read()  process  await write()               │   ║
║  │    ────────────────────────────────────────────────>                │   ║
║  │         │            │                     │                         │   ║
║  │         ▼            ▼                     ▼                         │   ║
║  │    [other tasks] [other tasks]        [other tasks]                 │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │    Event loop can run other coroutines during I/O!                  │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic File Operations

```python
import aiofiles
import asyncio

async def main():
    # Write to file
    async with aiofiles.open('example.txt', 'w') as f:
        await f.write("Hello, async world!\n")
        await f.write("Second line.\n")

    # Read from file
    async with aiofiles.open('example.txt', 'r') as f:
        content = await f.read()
        print(f"Content:\n{content}")

    # Read line by line
    async with aiofiles.open('example.txt', 'r') as f:
        async for line in f:
            print(f"Line: {line.strip()}")

    # Append to file
    async with aiofiles.open('example.txt', 'a') as f:
        await f.write("Appended line.\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: Parallel File Operations

```python
import aiofiles
import asyncio
import os

async def read_file(filepath):
    """Read a file asynchronously"""
    async with aiofiles.open(filepath, 'r') as f:
        return await f.read()

async def write_file(filepath, content):
    """Write to a file asynchronously"""
    async with aiofiles.open(filepath, 'w') as f:
        await f.write(content)

async def copy_file(src, dst):
    """Copy file asynchronously"""
    content = await read_file(src)
    await write_file(dst, content)

async def main():
    # Create test files
    for i in range(5):
        await write_file(f'file_{i}.txt', f'Content of file {i}\n' * 100)

    # Read all files in parallel
    files = [f'file_{i}.txt' for i in range(5)]
    tasks = [read_file(f) for f in files]
    contents = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

    for filepath, content in zip(files, contents):
        print(f"{filepath}: {len(content)} bytes")

    # Cleanup
    for f in files:
        os.remove(f)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic httpx Usage

```python
import httpx
import asyncio

async def main():
    # Simple request
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        # GET
        response = await client.get('http://httpbin.org/get')
        print(f"Status: {response.status_code}")
        print(f"JSON: {response.json()['url']}")

        # POST
        response = await client.post(
            'http://httpbin.org/post',
            json={'key': 'value'}
        )
        print(f"Posted: {response.json()['json']}")

        # With timeout
        response = await client.get(
            'http://httpbin.org/delay/1',
            timeout=5.0
        )
        print(f"Delayed response: {response.status_code}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: HTTP/2 and Streaming

```python
import httpx
import asyncio

async def main():
    # HTTP/2 client
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True) as client:
        response = await client.get('https://www.google.com')
        print(f"HTTP version: {response.http_version}")

    # Streaming download
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        async with client.stream('GET', 'http://httpbin.org/bytes/1000') as response:
            total = 0
            async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                total += len(chunk)
                print(f"Received {len(chunk)} bytes (total: {total})")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: WebSocket Client

```python
import asyncio
import websockets

async def client():
    uri = "ws://echo.websocket.org"

    async with websockets.connect(uri) as websocket:
        # Send message
        await websocket.send("Hello, WebSocket!")
        print(f"Sent: Hello, WebSocket!")

        # Receive response
        response = await websocket.recv()
        print(f"Received: {response}")

        # Send multiple messages
        for i in range(3):
            message = f"Message {i}"
            await websocket.send(message)
            response = await websocket.recv()
            print(f"Echo: {response}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(client())
```

#### Example 2: WebSocket Server

```python
import asyncio
import websockets
import json

connected_clients = set()

async def handler(websocket, path):
    """Handle WebSocket connections"""
    connected_clients.add(websocket)
    print(f"Client connected. Total: {len(connected_clients)}")

    try:
        async for message in websocket:
            data = json.loads(message)
            print(f"Received: {data}")

            # Broadcast to all clients
            for client in connected_clients:
                if client != websocket:
                    await client.send(json.dumps({
                        'type': 'broadcast',
                        'message': data['message']
                    }))

            # Echo back
            await websocket.send(json.dumps({
                'type': 'echo',
                'message': data['message']
            }))

    except websockets.ConnectionClosed:
        pass
    finally:
        connected_clients.remove(websocket)
        print(f"Client disconnected. Total: {len(connected_clients)}")

async def main():
    async with websockets.serve(handler, "localhost", 8765):
        print("WebSocket server started on ws://localhost:8765")
        await asyncio.Future()  # Run forever

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: asyncpg (PostgreSQL)

```python
import asyncio
import asyncpg

async def main():
    # Create connection
    conn = await asyncpg.connect(
        host='localhost',
        port=5432,
        user='postgres',
        password='password',
        database='testdb'
    )

    try:
        # Create table
        await conn.execute('''
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
                name VARCHAR(100),
                email VARCHAR(100)
            )
        ''')

        # Insert data
        await conn.execute('''
            INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ($1, $2)
        ''', 'Alice', 'alice@example.com')

        # Query data
        rows = await conn.fetch('SELECT * FROM users')
        for row in rows:
            print(f"User: {row['name']}, Email: {row['email']}")

        # Single row
        row = await conn.fetchrow(
            'SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', 'Alice'
        )
        print(f"Found: {row['email']}")

    finally:
        await conn.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: Connection Pool

```python
import asyncio
import asyncpg

async def get_user(pool, user_id):
    """Get user using connection from pool"""
    async with pool.acquire() as conn:
        return await conn.fetchrow(
            'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', user_id
        )

async def main():
    # Create connection pool
    pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(
        host='localhost',
        port=5432,
        user='postgres',
        password='password',
        database='testdb',
        min_size=5,     # Minimum connections
        max_size=20,    # Maximum connections
    )

    try:
        # Parallel queries using pool
        tasks = [get_user(pool, i) for i in range(1, 11)]
        users = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

        for user in users:
            if user:
                print(f"User: {user['name']}")

    finally:
        await pool.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: Async database connection pool
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  req["many concurrent requests"] --> acq["async with pool.acquire()"]
  acq --> pool[("asyncpg pool — min 5, max 20")]
  pool --> db[("PostgreSQL")]
  acq -->|"pool exhausted"| wait["task waits without blocking the loop"]
diagrams.explain: The pool bounds how many connections each process opens. Size it from the database side: workers × max pool size must stay under the server's connection limit, otherwise adding replicas of your service takes the database down.

sections.title: 13.6 Redis with aioredis
sections.body:
### Code Example

```python
import asyncio
import aioredis

async def main():
    # Connect to Redis
    redis = await aioredis.from_url("redis://localhost")

    try:
        # String operations
        await redis.set("key", "value")
        value = await redis.get("key")
        print(f"String: {value}")

        # List operations
        await redis.rpush("mylist", "item1", "item2", "item3")
        items = await redis.lrange("mylist", 0, -1)
        print(f"List: {items}")

        # Hash operations
        await redis.hset("user:1", mapping={"name": "Alice", "age": 30})
        user = await redis.hgetall("user:1")
        print(f"Hash: {user}")

        # Pub/Sub
        pubsub = redis.pubsub()
        await pubsub.subscribe("channel")

        # Publish in separate task
        async def publisher():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            await redis.publish("channel", "Hello!")

        asyncio.create_task(publisher())

        # Receive message
        async for message in pubsub.listen():
            if message['type'] == 'message':
                print(f"Received: {message['data']}")
                break

    finally:
        await redis.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

sections.title: Pitfalls & Gotchas
sections.body:
### Session Reuse

```python
import aiohttp
import asyncio

# ❌ Creating new session per request (slow!)
async def bad_fetch(url):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as resp:
            return await resp.text()

# ✅ Reuse session
async def good_fetch(session, url):
    async with session.get(url) as resp:
        return await resp.text()

async def main():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        urls = [f"http://example.com/page{i}" for i in range(100)]
        tasks = [good_fetch(session, url) for url in urls]
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
```

### Connection Pool Exhaustion

```python
# ❌ Too many concurrent connections
async def bad():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        tasks = [session.get(url) for url in urls]  # 10000 connections!
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

# ✅ Use semaphore to limit
async def good():
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(100)  # Max 100 concurrent

    async def fetch(session, url):
        async with sem:
            async with session.get(url) as resp:
                return await resp.text()

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        tasks = [fetch(session, url) for url in urls]
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
```

sections.title: Performance Notes
sections.body:
| Library  | Use Case            | Performance     |
| -------- | ------------------- | --------------- |
| aiohttp  | HTTP client/server  | ~10k req/s      |
| httpx    | Modern HTTP, HTTP/2 | ~5k req/s       |
| asyncpg  | PostgreSQL          | ~100k queries/s |
| aioredis | Redis               | ~100k ops/s     |
